rows.11:1400:
You know the soccer club is split into a first team and a second team, don't you?
And the second-team players, which is to say people like us, were made to hold a training camp at school.
Of course, we didn't get the same treatment or standing as the first team's core players, the regulars included.
First-team players don't stay overnight at school.
We hardly ever even got to see them.
However you looked at it, we had neither the talent nor the grit to move up to the first team.
If anything, rather than getting stronger or winning tournaments, I'd have been happy just to have fun in club activities.
But according to the first-team people, that makes you a loser.
The second team is a bunch of losers like that.
Players get dropped from the first team to the second, but almost nobody ever moves up from the second to the first.
But for me, that actually made it easier.
So what if you're a loser, as long as you're having fun?{p}
rows.11:17ac:
...I see.
So you're on a different side from me, {a}.{p}
rows.11:23e0:
"...Looks like this is the only spot."
With that, Sodeyama tossed his bag up onto the top bunk of a bed far from the entrance.
The bed to its right was empty.
"Then I'll take this one."
I put my things on the bed to the right of the one Sodeyama had chosen.
"...Hey, that guy picked bed number 4."
"...Yeah.
What an idiot."
I didn't miss the two guys whispering to each other nearby.{p}
rows.11:2894:
From that day on, the grueling practices began.
But after dinner we had free time, so we could relax.
Everyone had brought handheld video game consoles or portable CD players.
Those who hadn't brought them had manga or novels, or cards and games instead, and everyone passed the time in their own way on their beds.
Sodeyama and I talked about all sorts of things, our studies and our hobbies.
Good times always fly by.{p}
rows.11:30fc:
Days like that went on for a while.
And day by day, Sodeyama's health and color got worse.
He looked as if you couldn't tell whether he was alive or dead.
And along with it, the bruise on his right hand grew bigger too, stamping its mark ever more clearly, a dark, murky black.{p}
rows.11:3998:
...But what I'd taken for a blanket was a living thing.
A nameless, caterpillar-like creature, its whole body wrapped in a pale brown, blanket-like cloth, was lying over Sodeyama.
"Ah!"
I cried out before I could stop myself.
The instant I did, the thing stopped moving.{p}
rows.11:3dd0:
Then all of a sudden, it opened its mouth wide.
It was a mouth so huge it looked like it could swallow a human head in one gulp.
...I couldn't run away.
Strangely, I even forgot to run.
Fear had frozen me in place, and tangled up with it was the shock of meeting something unknown; between them, my five senses were stolen from me.
It kept glaring at me, its huge mouth still wide open.{p}I couldn't run away. What do you think I did?
rows.11:3fc8: I don't know what came over me myself, but I spat.{p}
rows.11:4530:
Even if I told anyone what happened to Sodeyama, there was no way they'd believe me.
So I kept quiet.
But even if I kept quiet, the fact remained that Sodeyama had disappeared, and I was the one who'd been with him until the end, so I figured I'd be questioned.
But nothing happened.
The moment it came out that Sodeyama had been sleeping in bed number 4, I was called in by the principal.{p}
rows.11:508c:
...That's right, inside the lodge.
Believe it or not, he'd been in the soccer club, the same as me.
Well, he'd already graduated by the time I joined, so I never met him.
Anyway, about this Reaper Pencil.
They say that if you use it, you can do automatic writing.
The pencil's power moves your hand on its own, and it writes out a certain message.
Now, about that message.
Apparently it reveals the very thing that will get the person using the Reaper Pencil killed.
For example, 'running out into the road,' or 'getting into a fight with someone'...
They say it's a pencil that can predict that kind of thing.
What I'm going to tell you is something that happened involving this Reaper Pencil.
It was last summer.
During the soccer club's training camp, a boy found the Reaper Pencil.
His name was Michio Yamamoto.{p}
rows.11:78b0:
Something like human hair.
And it crossed my mind.
Could this be...
Sodeyama's head...?
rows.11:868c:
Sodeyama tried to shove the Upside-Down Woman away.
But he was so tense that there was no strength in his hands.
The Upside-Down Woman glared at Sodeyama with bulging eyes and threatened him.
"Promise me, or I'll leave you covered in blood..."
Hearing that, Sodeyama made the promise.
That he wouldn't tell anyone he'd met the Upside-Down Woman.
But that voice of the Upside-Down Woman's...{p}
rows.11:87c4:
I see.
So that's the kind of story you like.
The story I'm about to tell is meant for someone exactly like you.
First, before I tell you about the thing I mentioned that appears in the lodge, there's something I need to tell you.
Listen carefully.
It's about the habits of insects.
You know... when people keep or catch bugs, they use a bug cage, right?
And bugs that get shoved into a bug cage want to get out, don't they?
When that happens, some bugs try to push their heads through the bars of the cage.
A bug like that can't get its body out through the bars, so it tries to pull its head, which it went to all that trouble to get out, back into the cage.
And then...
Sometimes it can't pull it back in properly, it catches on the bars, and the bug's head comes right off.
The head that came off rolls outside the bars, and inside the cage lies a headless bug carcass.{p}
rows.11:a9ac:
"N-Naoko..."
Takeda was sitting on one of the beds.
"Why'd you go and run away from home?
You're getting us into all kinds of trouble."
"Yeah, hurry up and go home already."
Saying that, they laid into her and shoved her around.
Just then, they heard a cat.{p}
rows.11:afa4:
The next day, there was a search for the missing girls.
Witnesses said the girls had gone toward the lodge, and when people went looking there, they found bodies that looked as if animals had torn them apart and fed on them.
Officially, it was put down to wild dogs, but nothing about it added up.
Even now, students who stay there say they woke up in the morning with cat scratches, or heard cats crying.
When I was at training camp, I woke up in the morning and found cat scratches on me, so I quit the soccer club that same day.
I was convinced the rumors were true.
Hm? Takeda, you mean?
She graduated last year.
The story I just told you is only a rumor, after all.
But they say Takeda still comes to the lodge from time to time.
And that the cries of cats echo through the school at night.
Maybe someone else has become cat food again.
That's the end of my story.
Next, please.{p}
rows.11:bd40:
The next day, the bullies had vanished.
And strangely enough, there were exactly as many cats as there were missing girls.
The police searched for them, but they were never found.
In the end, it was decided they had run away from home.
Hm? The cats from that night, you mean?
They did nothing but cry, and people found them creepy, so no one would take them.
So they were taken to the pound.
I heard this later, but apparently those cats were handed over to a university hospital and became lab animals.
Do you know what they do to lab animals?
They make them sick on purpose, and dissect them without anesthesia.
Because, supposedly, with anesthesia they can't get accurate data.
What? You don't think that's disgusting?
{a}, go look into it yourself. Lab animals.
If you go to the library, you'll find out.
It's beyond anything you can imagine.
And what's more, those lab animals used to be human..................
That's what I think, anyway.
Because they appear, you see. In the lodge...
The ghosts of those girls, with their bellies ripped open, or turned into specimens.
When I heard that story, I quit the soccer club.
I don't want to stay overnight in that lodge.
If you think it's just a rumor, why don't you try staying there yourself?
Still, I think that's the reason so many people quit the athletic clubs after summer vacation.
Well, anyway, I'll end my story here.
I'd rather not picture it too much.
Next, please.{p}
rows.11:ca80:
As soon as Takeda answered, she suddenly vanished, cats and all.
A few cats were left behind where she had been.
"C-cats..."
"Wh-what do we do?"
"But if we don't keep our promise......."
Each of them took one cat home.{p}
